svg.text: Social media: the nurse's public uniform

g.text: NO PATIENTS
no names, faces,
stories, wards!
"ANONYMOUS" LIES
details identify —
don't post it!
PAUSE RULE
panel + grandma +
patient test!
BOUNDARIES
no patient friend-reqs,
separate accounts!
POST GOOD
educate, celebrate,
advocate — proudly!
5 RULES: zero patient content + de-identification never trusted + pause-before-post +
firm boundaries + positive professional voice. Screenshots outlive deletions — post like the
N&MC, your patient and your grandmother read everything.
"BUT I HID THE NAME!" — ward + diagnosis + date + age = identified. "Funny story about a
patient today…" = breach + cruelty + virality. Colleagues identifiable? Same rules. Uniform
selfies inside wards? Check policy — backgrounds leak patients.
PAUSE TEST (before EVERY work post): would I say it on TV in uniform? Would the patient
smile reading it? Would the panel applaud? Any NO = delete the draft. Angry posting after
shifts? Sleep first — rage-posts end careers ("my hospital kills people" = investigation).
BOUNDARIES: decline patient/relative friend-requests kindly ("I keep social media separate
— reach me via the clinic line"); separate personal/professional accounts; privacy settings
high; never discuss cases in DMs. Friended your ward crush-patient? Unfriend + reflect.
CYBERBULLYING: screenshot, block, report (platform + facility + police if threats). Bullied
colleague? Support + report — silence enables (PRO-I courage!). Never retaliate-post.
POST GOOD: myth-busting threads, vaccination drives, graduation joy, CPD certificates,
hand-hygiene dances (consented colleagues only!) — build the profession's brand + YOUR hireable
footprint. Employers google you: let them find a nurse.
MANTRA: "in uniform online, always — patients never, pride always."
